claims.statement: A blue starting technology is the common route toward Gravity Drive, while Sarween Tools is a defensible yellow start when the slice supports its economy or a later Helios route.
claims.conditions: Choose after inspecting the slice, tech skips, desired faction-tech route, and availability of a Technology follow.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; Thunder’s Edge discussed; exact current ruleset unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts disagree in emphasis and call the analysis preliminary. ASR renders some technology names inconsistently.

claims.statement: Plan movement out of the home nebula around the cruiser’s reduced natural movement; later bonuses may still matter.
claims.conditions: Applies to ships leaving the home system, especially the opening expansion and a later large fleet; account for available movement bonuses.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; Thunder’s Edge discussed; exact current ruleset unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Podcast rules paraphrase, not a current-rules check.

claims.statement: Use the home space station’s commodity-value increase and its access to other station controllers as possible trade routes.
claims.conditions: The bonus is useful only if other stations are present or ordinary partners are reachable; the home cruiser’s movement can constrain adjacency.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; Thunder’s Edge discussed; exact current ruleset unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Station trading text is paraphrased from ASR and rules compatibility is unreviewed.

claims.statement: Track Liberate’s infantry condition and, in most cases, resolve its readying before exploration so an attachment does not raise the planet’s resource value first.
claims.conditions: On gaining control, the hosts describe readying when infantry meet the planet’s resource value and otherwise placing an infantry; evaluate the actual planet and current card text.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; Thunder’s Edge discussed; exact current ruleset unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The exact ability wording and timing are based on the hosts’ preliminary rules reading; no legality review was performed.

claims.statement: Inspect slice planets, skips, resource and influence yield, and infantry routes before settling on an opening plan.
claims.conditions: The hosts consider early slice quality unusually consequential because it shapes Liberate value and later economic tempo.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; tournament-slice discussion is illustrative, not universal.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts call the faction draft-sensitive; slice examples are not tested prescriptions.

claims.statement: When the round-one choice is between early plastic and Technology, the hosts favor plastic because it expands access to planets and compounds the weak starting economy.
claims.conditions: A priority rather than a mandatory pick; depends on slice, available follows and whether early Technology is actually usable.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; Thunder’s Edge discussed; exact current ruleset unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: One host initially favors tech experimentation, then agrees plastic is the safer priority; preserve this changed emphasis.

claims.statement: Consider Construction, Trade and Warfare as high-value round-one tools, adjusting their relative priority to the slice and card timing.
claims.conditions: Construction adds a dock/build opportunity; Trade funds the weak economy; Warfare may improve expansion. Other players’ picks and the table determine access.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; strategic opinions only.
claims.uncertainty: The episode contains a card-by-card debate and no universal ranking.

claims.statement: Do not make round-one Politics or a Custodians rush the default; the hosts prefer early development and a later Imperial opportunity.
claims.conditions: Applies as abstract advice when the slice and tempo do not already make a rush feasible; scoring access and table conditions can change the choice.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; opinion, not rules guidance.
claims.uncertainty: Strong host recommendation based on preliminary experience; not an objective evaluation.

claims.statement: Construction can establish another Helios dock and add production near a valuable planet or a useful infantry build.
claims.conditions: Most attractive when placement helps a nearby expansion/build plan; the hosts caution that a second dock may not be immediately usable without money and tokens.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; exact current ruleset unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Specific placement value is slice-dependent.

claims.statement: Take Trade when it produces accessible, timely money; the home station does not guarantee a reachable trading partner.
claims.conditions: Check whether station holders are in the game, adjacency and movement, trade timing, and local washing norms before relying on Trade to fund the opening.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; strategic advice only.
claims.uncertainty: Actual table economy varies substantially.

claims.statement: Warfare can rescue a poor slice by adding infantry and enabling a more valuable second expansion route.
claims.conditions: The hosts give the example of a slice where nearby planets cannot be liberated efficiently; compare with Construction and the table’s Warfare timing.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; strategy example only.
claims.uncertainty: The recommendation is explicitly situational.

claims.statement: The common technology path starts blue and reaches Gravity Drive and ship upgrades; a yellow start into Sarween is reasonable when the slice supports it.
claims.conditions: If the breakthrough is acquired, the hosts consider AI Development Algorithm and Helios V2; without it they describe a yellow route before blue movement tech. Prerequisite access matters.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; Thunder’s Edge discussed; current legality unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Two hosts offer distinct paths and their prerequisite phrasing contains ASR noise.

claims.statement: Integrated Economy can combine expansion and production when the slice supplies the required skips and the player can time Technology and Liberate around the sequence.
claims.conditions: The example depends on Sarween, a double-yellow skip such as Tiamat, an available Technology primary and a planet route; the guest does not recommend it every game.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; map example is not a universal line.
claims.uncertainty: The other host regards the prerequisite combination as a substantial, slice-specific ask.

claims.statement: Treat Helios V2 as a major technology goal when extra planet value and production can repair the economy and support a defended position.
claims.conditions: The hosts favor it over speculative tech in many games, while recognizing prerequisites and the opportunity cost of movement or other upgrades.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; component text and rules are not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: Strong but preliminary host opinion; exact production figures in speech are not treated as verified rules.

claims.statement: Galvanize surviving units after combat and focus its additional combat or ability die where it helps win a key fight or hold ground.
claims.conditions: Phoenix Standard can galvanize a participating unit at combat’s end; a unit destroyed before the effect cannot benefit, and tokens are finite commitments.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; exact token handling and card text unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts describe seven tokens but note an active question about what happens when they run out; token movement is not assumed.

claims.statement: Build toward a midgame Mecatol Rex ground position; the hosts see the faction’s strengths as more reliable there than in an early Fracture expedition.
claims.conditions: Requires solving early economy, movement and ground-force needs first; the speakers allow a Fracture attempt when tempo and position support it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; strategic thesis, not a guaranteed scoring route.
claims.uncertainty: The source calls its endgame example unusually favorable and anecdotal.

claims.statement: Proxima Targeting VI is situationally valuable for a prepared, prolonged ground defense with galvanized units concentrated at an important system; its interaction with X-89 remains unresolved in the episode.
claims.conditions: Consider only when the player already expects a consequential ground battle or repeated defense; setup and concentration are required.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; hosts explicitly lack a settled ruling for X-89 interaction.
claims.uncertainty: The tech is debated; the early X-89 discussion is speculative and the source references a tournament FAQ without resolving it.

claims.statement: Treat the Egeiro as an occasional forward production or replacement option rather than an automatic flagship purchase.
claims.conditions: The hosts like its one-unit production for rebuilding a carrier or adding a small unit at a forward location; its cost, movement and single die limit appeal.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; current unit values unreviewed.
claims.uncertainty: One host reports never building it in research games; the favorable examples are hypothetical.

claims.statement: The mech and hero can deter or punish a costly attack, but the hosts question how often the mech’s same-system infantry trigger and limited tokens will pay off and leave some hero target/value questions open.
claims.conditions: Use as a possible defensive closer when galvanized units and ground forces already occupy the threatened system; verify targeting and timing before relying on a specific hero kill.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; Thunder’s Edge guide contains unresolved rules questions.
claims.uncertainty: ASR corrupts the hero name in places; printed value versus modified combat result is debated and no ruling is established.

claims.statement: Dame Briar can galvanize another unit of the same player in the destroyed unit’s system after that player’s unit is destroyed; the hosts suggest this as a flexible way to reach Nip and Tuck’s three-galvanized-unit unlock and value its Sabotage protection.
claims.conditions: An agent use may help another player in the immediate combat; unlock timing depends on three galvanized units being present, and the commander’s value rises when a decisive action card is available.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; commander and agent effects are paraphrased, not rules-verified.
claims.uncertainty: The source expresses confusion about the Necrovirus clause and timing; no strategy is inferred for that clause.

claims.statement: Offer Raise the Standard and the Alliance early when the return funds Last Bastion’s weak opening, but account for the rival action-card protection granted by a later Alliance sale.
claims.conditions: Price against timing and what the proceeds unlock; the hosts favor early liquidity and become more cautious once their own economy is established.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; trade advice is table-specific.
claims.uncertainty: Transaction prices are illustrative bargaining examples, not stable valuations.

claims.statement: Set Alliance price by whether the deal gets the player economically online; blue-skip or faction-ability swaps can be attractive, but consider whether the buyer is a dangerous rival.
claims.conditions: The speakers float roughly three to four trade goods in one round-one case and around six or a Support for the Throne in a round-two case; they condition value on timing, slice and what the buyer can do.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; the prices are examples from one table discussion.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts disagree only by emphasis on exact valuation; market, buyer and game state dominate.

claims.statement: Treat named tournament-slice lines as examples of the faction’s map dependence rather than as a repeatable opening recipe.
claims.conditions: The examples rely on exact skips, system distances, planet values, movement and Warfare timing; a different draft changes the line.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; slice observations from the recording’s tournament environment.
claims.uncertainty: ASR garbles several proper names; only the general conditional lesson is retained.

claims.statement: The hosts see no dependable objective specialty; they recommend solving the early economy and taking an actual scoring opportunity when the position is ready.
claims.conditions: Mecatol and Imperial are focal points in their discussion, but scoring still depends on revealed objectives, timing, position and opponents.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; guide opinion, no objective performance study.
claims.uncertainty: The conclusion is broad and based on preliminary play experience.

claims.statement: A prepared, fortified endgame can make a table-wide win-slay difficult, but opponents can exploit the weak opening before the faction’s combat closers are established.
claims.conditions: The defensive example assumes enough economy, ground forces, galvanized units, position and scoring tempo; it is not immunity or a guaranteed win.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 441, published 2026-01-28; based on anecdotal games and host speculation.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts describe an unusually favorable game and acknowledge the setup can fail early.

connections.conditions: The guide’s conditional line needs the relevant prerequisites, a timely Technology primary, and a planet that can be readied before the follow-on production; it is not a default build path.
At the end of combat, Phoenix Standard is described as one route to galvanizing a surviving participating unit; it does not require a win.
The speakers connect concentrated galvanized units with Proxima’s long ground-defense use case; the tech is situational and the X-89 interaction remains unresolved.
The hosts speculate that losing a galvanized mech can set up the hero’s destruction effect in the same system; target and combat-value details are not resolved.
